subject: Next steps: HealthCentric trial objectives, timeline & readout scheduling
messages:
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: Emma Jones <emma.jones@healthcentric.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 8 Jan 2026 15:23:00 +0000
Subject: Recap + proposed trial scope for HealthCentric

Hi Emma — thanks again for taking the time earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side so we have alignment before we draft a short mutual action plan.

Call summary (high level):
- Primary goal: accelerate triage workflows by surfacing concise, structured summaries from clinician notes and intake forms.
- Key metrics you mentioned: average time saved per case, precision of suggested codes, and false-positive rate for recommended actions.
- Security and data flow: HealthCentric will run sample data in your VPC; Redwood will provide a private deployment (dedicated) option. SOC2 evidence will be shared once NDA is executed.

Proposed 4-week trial (draft):
1) Week 0: Kickoff + data onboarding (SFTP or secure share).
2) Week 1–2: Model tuning and integration (batch + API).
3) Week 3: Evaluation run against 200 sample cases + metric collection.
4) Week 4: Final readout + decision window (go/no-go).

Success criteria (please confirm / adjust):
- Summary precision >= 85% (clinician validation sample)
- Time savings >= 20% on average per case
- System latency for API < 300ms p50 for single-request flow

Owners: Redwood: Sean (integration/infra), Marcus (eval & metrics). HealthCentric: Emma (project lead), suggested reviewer: Dr. Patel (clinical lead).

I attached a short outline (healthcentric-poc-outline.pdf) to use as the basis for a mutual-action plan. Can you confirm the success metrics above and availability for a kickoff next week? If those look good we'll send a concise M.A.P. and propose a readout week (we suggest Feb 9–13 for exec slot).

Thanks — Rachel
Rachel Kim
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
rachel.kim@redwood.com | (415) 555-0182

Attachment: healthcentric-poc-outline.pdf (1 page)
From: Emma Jones <emma.jones@healthcentric.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Cc: HealthCentric Evaluation Team <it@healthcentric.com>
Date: Thu, 8 Jan 2026 19:07:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Recap + proposed trial scope for HealthCentric

Rachel — really appreciate the clear notes. Quick responses inline: 

Summary: yep, accurate.
Success metrics: Sounds reasonable, with two clarifications:
- Precision: we care more about clinically actionable accuracy (so please surface both exact-match and clinical-acceptability in the final report).
- Time savings: 20% minimum is fine, but would like to capture median and 75th percentile as well.

Timeline: 4-week trial looks doable. Kickoff next Wednesday (Jan 14) at 10am PT would work for our project leads.

Stakeholders: adding our clinical lead (Dr. Ravi Patel) to shortlist — I'll intro him on kickoff invite.

Legal/Procurement: we'll need a brief SOW and an LOI for sign-off; procurement handles the rapid PO once terms are set.

Thanks — Emma
Emma Jones
Director of Clinical Ops, HealthCentric
emma.jones@healthcentric.com | +1 (617) 555-0123
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: Emma Jones <emma.jones@healthcentric.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 9 Jan 2026 02:15:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Recap + proposed trial scope for HealthCentric

Thanks Emma — great, Jan 14 10am PT is on our calendar. I've pulled together a compact trial playbook (see summary below) and attached a one-sheet MAP with owners and milestones (mutual-action-plan.xlsx). Please flag anything missing.

Trial playbook (concise):
- Pre-kickoff (by Jan 13): SFTP credentials or secure share, sample dataset (200 de-identified cases), contacts for dev/infra.
- Kickoff (Jan 14): 30–45m technical + stakeholder alignment. Agenda: goals, success criteria, access, timeline.
- Integration window (Jan 15–23): Redwood will deploy a dedicated inference endpoint in your VPC; Sean will own environment setup and access.
- Eval run (Jan 24–28): Redwood runs the 200-case evaluation; Marcus will deliver a results package (metrics + error analysis).
- Readout prep (Jan 29–Feb 4): internal review and slide deck prep.
- Exec readout (proposed Feb 9): 30m slot for go/no-go decision with your VP of Product.

Metrics & gating:
- Primary: clinical-acceptability (binary sample review) >= 85%
- Secondary: median time savings >= 20% and p75 savings reported
- Non-functional: p50 latency < 300ms, uptime during eval > 99.5%

Owners (Redwood):
- Sean Gallagher — infra & VPC deployment (contact: sean.gallagher@redwood.com)
- Marcus Lin — evaluation framework & metrics (contact: marcus.lin@redwood.com)

Next steps from Redwood:
1) Finalize MAP and send calendar invites for kickoff + provisional exec readout.
2) Share SOC2 summary + security questionnaire before data onboarding.
3) Draft LOI for your legal/procurement to review; we'll aim to keep it short and carve the procurement step into post-readout PO execution.

On the legal front — we can have a short draft LOI ready by Jan 16; would that timeline work?

Best — Rachel

Subject: Re: Next steps: HealthCentric trial objectives, timeline & readout scheduling

Quick alignment notes — adding a few specifics so we don't miss anything during the kick: 

Evaluation details:
- We'll provide an evaluation harness that produces: exact-match, clinical-acceptability (manual sample), latency distributions, and a short error taxonomy (FP/over-summarization/missing-entities).
- Suggest HealthCentric team perform the manual clinical-acceptability review on a 50-case random sample (we'll seed the sample).

Deliverables to HealthCentric after eval:
- Results package (CSV + dashboard link)
- Short slide deck highlighting strengths, gaps, and recommended next steps

On presenters for the exec readout: I'd like to present the metric readouts and proposed next-phase recommendations. Sean to present deployment posture and SLOs. Rachel — can you own scheduling the VP-level slot and procurement handoff?

I'll prep the dashboard template ahead of the eval.
Marcus
Director, Applied ML | Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.com
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: Emma Jones <emma.jones@healthcentric.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Jan 2026 11:02:00 +0000
Subject: Finalize: exec readout timing & LOI next steps

Hi Emma — looping back after our internal prep. We're locking in the final pieces so procurement can move quickly post-readout. A few asks: 

1) Can you confirm whether Feb 9 or Feb 11 works better for a 30-minute exec readout? We can do 8–11am PT on either day; if neither fits, please propose a 45-minute slot the week of Feb 9.
2) Who on your side will be the signatory for the LOI / initial purchase order? Procurement team or VP Product? We ask because it affects the LOI recipient and level of detail.
3) We'll send a concise LOI via DocuSign (link will be shared by Jan 26) covering the trial scope, data access notes, and acceptance criteria. Is it okay to copy your procurement contact once we send it?

DocuSign preview link: https://www.docusign.com/12345/HC-POC-LOI (preview)
HubSpot playbook: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/123456/company/HealthCentric

If everything looks good I'll: 1) send the kickoff invite for Jan 14 10am PT, 2) circulate the LOI draft on Jan 16, and 3) put a tentative exec readout on Feb 9 pending your confirmation.

Thanks — Rachel
Rachel Kim
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
